This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. The community of Bend, Oregon is grieving
after yesterday's shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School. The teenage shooter fired
into a special needs classroom. He killed three children, ages 5, 8, and 11, and a 25-year-old
teacher, Megan Lambert. Melanie Keebler is the mayor of Bend.
It is just an incredible and profound moment of grief and overwhelm for people. It's hard
to process these kinds of things. It's unfathomable that people would lose their children in this
manner when schools are supposed to be a place where people can teach our children and they
can feel safe.
Police say a teacher threw her phone at the gunman, then tackled and fought him, likely
saving lives. He was shot dead by a man who followed him into the building.
President Trump is pausing a new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy. He
told Congress the move was in the national interest. The bill was named after the late
South Carolina Republican Senator Lindsey Graham. It sought to clamp down on the flow
of money fueling the war against Ukraine. It comes a week after Trump said the U.S. had
agreed to purchase diesel fuel from Russia to try to bring down global energy prices
despite international pressure to sanction Russia.
President Trump's campaign push ahead of the midterms took him to northwest Georgia today
to rally for the Republican Senate nominee, Congressman Mike Collins. Trump attacked a
rising Democratic star and rekindled his false claims about the 2020 elections. Raul Bali
of member station WABE reports.
Trump bounced from topic to topic during his roughly 90-minute speech that included several
attacks on U.S. Senator John Ossoff, the only Democratic senator up for reelection this
year in a state Trump won in 2024.
He does not represent your values and he never won the election. He was in there as an impostor.
Trump referring to the 2020 elections, which he continues to falsely claim he won in Georgia
along with falsely claiming that then Senator David Perdue won rather than Ossoff.
The president stopped short of making any claims on election security related to this
year. For NPR News, I'm Raul Bali in Dalton, Georgia.
Firefighters in southern California are battling several wildfires fueled by dry, windy weather.
The Norte Fire in Orange County has spread to several homes from member station LAist
Lucas Brady Woods reports.
The biggest fire in the region, the Henderson Fire, has burned over 2,000 acres near U.S.
Marine Base Camp Pendleton, south of LA.
Fires in Malibu and Orange County have prompted evacuations. Pauline McGee with the LA County
Fire Department says the biggest concern is wind spreading the fires into neighborhoods.
"Ambros can get into your small vents, windows, and that's how homes typically catch on fire."
High winds have driven some of the region's most destructive fires, including the deadly
Los Angeles wildfires last year.
For NPR News, I'm Lucas Brady Woods in Los Angeles.
Clothes lower on Wall Street today, this is NPR News.
New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani and city Democrats are urging private parking lot owners to block
federal immigration officers from using their properties. The plea follows the shooting
of a 28-year-old during an arrest last week. Federal officers had used a nearby private
lot as a staging area. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson defended the agency's
actions.
While Nino's effects are being felt on the west coast, communities are reeling from coastal
flooding across Southern California and parts of the Bay Area, Ezra David Romero of Member
Station KQED explains.
Scientists say the recent flooding is partly due to what they call a Kelvin wave. But this
massive wave isn't visible like a tsunami. It moves slowly beneath the ocean's surface
and is one of the first effects of El Nino, where warm ocean water sloshes eastward.
Dylan Amaya studies marine extremes at North Carolina State University.
This is not totally unexpected, but we expect five, maybe six of these coastally trapped
waves over the life of the El Nino event into the winter.
Kelvin waves can temporarily raise sea levels by several inches to more than a foot and
trigger minor flooding. Scientists say another Kelvin wave is crawling up the Mexico coast
and could reach California in the coming weeks.
For NPR News, I'm Ezra David Romero in San Francisco.
Brazil's government says that annual deforestation in the Amazon has fallen to its lowest level
since 1988. The rainforest lost about 1,300 square miles from August 2025 through July
2026, and it's a lot less than it did during the surge under former President Jair Bolsonaro
during his presidency, deforestation increased by about 60 percent. It's NPR.
